Kiln Field Bothy Association — Committee Minutes, 14 March

Present: the warden, the treasurer, and four members. The warden reported that the sleeping loft had been oversubscribed on six nights over the winter, and asked the committee to restate how places are allotted when more people arrive than the loft will hold. The committee confirmed the settled practice: walkers arriving on foot are accommodated before those arriving by bicycle, and cyclists before parties travelling by road vehicle. Nobody is turned away from the shelter of the ground room in any case, and the stove remains available to all present. The treasurer noted that the donation tin had covered the winter's coal with a little over. Next meeting 9 June at the same hour.

before:
Tidewell Harbour Office — Slipway Operating Manual, Section 4

Section 4 covers use of the concrete slipway between the fuel berth and the eastern wall. The winch is worked by the duty hand alone. Vehicles descend in low gear and reverse under the guidance of a second person standing on the apron, clear of the wire. Trailers may be left on the upper apron for up to two hours while a launch is in progress. The gate key is drawn from the office and returned the same day. Users write the time of launch and of recovery in the ledger kept on the office sill, and the harbour master reads the ledger through each Friday afternoon before the weekend traffic begins.
after:

before:
Bay Ferry Service Handbook — Crossing Conditions

This section sets out the physical conditions of the crossing for the guidance of relief crew. The channel between the slip and the island runs roughly north-east and lies deepest against the island shore. The bar carries a little under a metre at mean low water springs, and the channel dries for about forty minutes either side of the low. The ebb sets hard across the moorings and runs strongest in the second hour. Crew should note that the wind funnels down the valley behind the slip and can be a full force stronger there than out in the roads. Timetable adjustments are issued separately by the office.

before:
Parish Burial Ground — Memorial Inspection Policy

Memorials in the burial ground are inspected on a five-year cycle by two people working together, one of whom holds the current certificate. Inspection goes forward thus: the inspector first photographs the stone where it stands, then tests it by hand pressure, then enters the finding on the form, and lastly fixes the warning label where the stone is found unsound. Stones judged unsound are laid flat only with the written agreement of the clerk and after the grave owner has been written to at the last known address. The cycle for the northern extension falls due in the spring following completion of the older ground.

before:
Millrace Aquarium — Annual Stocking Report

The report covers the twelve display tanks and the two quarantine tanks in the back room for the year to March. Stocking densities are worked out by the surface-area method given in the old society handbook, at one centimetre of fish to sixty square centimetres of water surface. On that footing the long tank on the landing sits at nine tenths of its figure and the corner tank slightly over, the excess accounted for by three fish awaiting rehoming. Losses over the year came to seven, five of them in quarantine and put down to the March power interruption. Water changes were made weekly throughout by the volunteer rota.

The registry lists the holdings carrying a right of grazing on the moor above the village, with the number of sheep attaching to each. Entries are brought up to date at the November sitting.
